authors: Zheng, Z., Zhong, Y., Ma, A. & Zhang, L.
title: Single-temporal supervised learning for universal remote sensing change detection
relevance: Removes the objection that blocked Q74. The CEOS protocol and He 2024 both say change should be mapped DIRECTLY rather than by differencing per-year maps, but direct change detection normally needs labelled bitemporal CHANGE pairs, which we do not have and cannot afford. STAR trains a change detector from SINGLE-TEMPORAL labels alone, constructing pseudo-bitemporal pairs from unpaired labelled images so that change supervision is generated from semantic labels only. We have exactly that input - one labelled year, 2020 - and nothing else. Peer-reviewed in IJCV, with a unified ChangeStar2 architecture covering binary, object and semantic change. This is the single most direct answer the loop has found to an architectural problem it identified two iterations ago.

authors: Peng, D., Liu, M., Zhang, Y. & Guan, H.
title: Toward label-efficient deep learning change detection for remote sensing imagery: a comprehensive review
relevance: Maps the whole label-efficient change-detection space into six schemes - semi-supervised, weakly supervised, self-supervised, active learning, few-shot and unsupervised - with systematic comparisons. Needed because our constraint is not merely 'few labels' but a specific and unusual shape: one labelled DATE, no labelled CHANGE, and 17 unlabelled acquisitions. This gives the taxonomy to place ourselves in and to check whether a cheaper scheme than STAR fits, rather than adopting the first method that matches. Peer-reviewed 2025, so it postdates most of what this loop has surveyed on the modelling side.
